name: Fields of the Nephilim
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Five men from Hertfordshire dressed like spaghetti-western gunslingers, rolled in flour and made goth heavier than it had ever been. Then Carl McCoy split the band at its peak and kept the name.

hero.by: Fields of the Nephilim at Amphi Festival, Cologne, 2017. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Jack the Ripper meets the Man With No Name
eras.text: Carl McCoy grew up in a strict religious household reading about the Nephilim, the angel-human giants of Genesis. In Stevenage he put a band around that idea, sewed his own hats and put out the first record himself, with no press, radio or PR behind it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · The Nefilim: History
years.h: McCoy, the Wright brothers and Tony Pettitt form a band in Stevenage
years.p: Carl McCoy sings, Paul Wright plays guitar, his brother Nod Wright drums, Tony Pettitt plays bass and Gary Wisker plays saxophone. The name comes from the Nephilim and the magnetic fields around the Earth.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · The Quietus · The Nefilim: History
years.h: Burning the Fields comes out on the band's own Tower label
years.p: The debut 12-inch EP is picked up fast by Jungle Records, who pay for the sessions that become Returning to Gehenna. Wisker and his saxophone leave; Peter Yates comes in as second guitarist.
years.xp: The Quietus's Ben Graham describes the early climb as the hard way: constant gigging, opening for anyone who would have them, and word of mouth. Jungle Records was the band's first real backer; a Jungle director managed them.

years.cap: Fields of the Nephilim, classic five-piece line-up
years.src: Louder: Fields Of The Nephilim: an interview · Louder: Police found
years.h: The look: charity-shop Victoriana, cowboy dusters and flour
years.p: The band couldn't look like a band, McCoy said, so they mixed Victorian clothes with a Sergio Leone vibe and covered it all in dirt. Clay dust at one photo shoot, then Mother's Pride flour for good.
years.xp:
"We hated glam bands, so we wanted to look as grimy as possible," McCoy told Metal Hammer. He made his own hats from top hats and Stetsons sewn together, and got his pale contact lenses from a man who made them for BBC dramas, so he'd look like a photo of his blond, pale-eyed grandfather.

Fans copied it, bringing flour to shows in plastic bags to throw in the air when the band walked on. At parties, McCoy said, you could tell the Nephilim had been there from the floury handprints on other people's jackets.

years.src: The Quietus · Louder: Police found · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Situation Two, the Beggars Banquet imprint, signs the band
years.p: The first singles are Power and Preacher Man, goth dancefloor fillers that the weekly press mostly compared, unfavourably, to [[The Sisters of Mercy|553d8166-27b0-49fe-b8e4-89a984e2c375]].
years.xp: McCoy never accepted the comparison. "I think calling us Sisters copyists was very unfair," he told Louder; he sang that low, he said, because he burnt his throat on hot food as a kid and couldn't talk for four weeks. He heard the band as "Pink Floyd mixed with the Velvets," with jazz from Paul Wright's training.

eras.title: Number 28, and 13 pounds of flour
eras.text: Two albums on Situation Two made the Nephilim the biggest new band left on a scene the music press had stopped taking seriously. Readers bought the records; Melody Maker ran a weekly joke column about the drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dawnrazor · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Dawnrazor opens with Ennio Morricone
years.p: The debut album samples the harmonica theme from Once Upon a Time in the West and tops the UK Indie chart. Kerrang! liked the idea of "Spaghetti-metal" more than the execution.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Blue Water sneaks into the UK singles chart at No. 75
years.p: The first Nephilim single to chart at all, and the start of a run of hits on an indie label.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Melody Maker invents The Nod Corner
years.p: A spoof weekly column, supposedly by drummer Nod Wright, casts McCoy as a prima donna bossing him around. Wright took it graciously, Wikipedia says.
years.xp: McCoy enjoyed it. "We used to like that! It was great, it was good fun," he told the Quietus, though he thought Nod, the youngest in the band, took it a bit personally.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Moonchild, named for a Crowley novel, reaches No. 28
years.p: The lead single from the second album is the band's biggest chart hit.

years.src: Louder: Police found · Louder: Fields Of The Nephilim: an interview · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Nottingham police arrest the band over a bag of flour
years.p: After a show at Rock City, a hotel cleaner finds a fan's bag of white powder and calls the police. Officers haul the band out of bed in handcuffs and search the tour bus.
years.xp:
The bus held 13 pounds of what police took for cocaine, McCoy told Louder; in a 2012 Metal Hammer interview he put it at 12. It was flour from the stage show, and NME ran the story on May 28 under "Flour power Neph 'busted'."

"They must have thought we were heavily into our baking!" McCoy said. "Still, it got us half a page in The Mirror."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Nephilim · The Quietus
years.h: Recorded in a courthouse where the condemned were hanged
years.p: The Nephilim was cut at the Justice Rooms in Somerset and debuted at No. 12 on the UK albums chart. McCoy still calls it one of his two favourites.
years.xp:
"The place had a really cool vibe," Pettitt recalled. The record pulls from Crowley (Moonchild, Love Under Will), Lovecraft's Cthulhu (The Watchman, Last Exit for the Lost) and The Name of the Rose, sampled at the start of Endemoniada.

McCoy told the Quietus it was the first album where the band really crafted a sound: Dawnrazor had just been the live set of two years, "bunged" on a record.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Ten minutes long, and it still goes Top 40
years.p: Psychonaut, a non-album single with a sequencer pulse, reaches No. 35. Its video continues the mini horror films the band had been making with director Richard Stanley.

eras.title: Up to Beggars Banquet, and out
eras.text: For the third album the band moved up from Situation Two to Beggars Banquet itself and brought in a Pink Floyd engineer. It was their most polished record and their last together: McCoy said he could feel the band getting too big.

years.src: Wikipedia: Carl McCoy
years.h: McCoy plays the desert nomad in Hardware
years.p: Richard Stanley, who directed the band's videos, casts McCoy as the scavenger who opens his sci-fi horror film.

years.src: Wikipedia: Elizium · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · Louder: Police found
years.h: Elizium: Andy Jackson produces, Aleister Crowley speaks
years.p: Pink Floyd engineer Andy Jackson replaces Bill Buchanan, and At the Gates of Silent Memory opens with Crowley reading his own 1920 recording. The album reaches No. 22.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it the band's best all-around album. For Her Light clipped the Top 40 in its first week, and a remixed Sumerland (Dreamed) reached No. 37 in November.

Around then [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] opened for the Nephilim at Brixton Academy, McCoy remembered, possibly at the band's first headline show there.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Two nights of the Festival of Fire at the Town & Country Club
years.p: The classic line-up's last shows, in London. They become the live album Earth Inferno and the video Visionary Heads.

years.big: "I liked the idea of being a culty act."
q: I never saw The Fields Of The Nephilim as a big brand.
years.src: Louder: Police found · The Nefilim: History · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: McCoy quits the band and takes the name
years.p: Carl McCoy, to Louder. With Elizium selling, he feared the band was heading for big commercial success, so he split it up.
years.xp:
Months in each other's pockets had worn down personal relationships, Louder reported, and McCoy wanted more control. "I never saw The Fields Of The Nephilim as a big brand," he said.

The other four kept playing together but dropped the name.

eras.title: Two bands from one
eras.text: Beggars Banquet kept both halves. Yates, Pettitt and the Wrights became Rubicon with a new singer; McCoy disappeared into a heavier, harder project with a respelled name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rubicon (English band) · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: The rest of the band becomes Rubicon
years.p: With singer Andy Delaney, Rubicon makes What Starts, Ends for Beggars Banquet, produced by Mark Freegard. Room 101 follows in 1995, then the band ends.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Nefilim · Louder: Fields Of The Nephilim: an interview
years.h: McCoy's Zoon arrives, years late and full of death metal
years.p: Recorded as The Nefilim, the album sat for years over disagreements with the label, McCoy said. Beggars finally released it in April 1996.
years.xp: McCoy started the project with multi-instrumentalist John "Capachino" Carter, then built a live band of Paul Miles, Simon Rippin and Cian Houchin. In Metal Hammer McCoy named Zoon and The Nephilim as "the only ones I go back to."

eras.title: The reunion that wasn't
eras.text: A full reunion of the original five was announced and rehearsed, and never happened. What came out instead was a single, a few festival shows, an album the band disowned, and in 2005 a record made by McCoy and one collaborator.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: McCoy and Pettitt announce the comeback at Germany's Zillo Festival
years.p: Fields of the Nephilim will return with the Wright brothers, and Nefilim will continue alongside. Members said they rehearsed and wrote, but the original line-up never made it back on stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · The Quietus
years.h: One More Nightmare (Trees Come Down) on Jungle Records
years.p: McCoy and Pettitt rework two songs from Burning the Fields for their old label, then play Roskilde, M'era Luna, Eurorock and Woodstage that summer.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Jungle releases Fallen, and the band disowns it
years.p: Built from 1997–2001 recordings, the reworked songs and a Nefilim demo. McCoy said Jungle put out unfinished tracks without his consent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mourning Sun · Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Fifteen years after Elizium, Mourning Sun
years.p: McCoy and Carter spent 18 months on it in McCoy's mobile studio, the Ice Cage, which went as far as Norway. Carter is the only other credited player; McCoy's daughters sing on the title track.
years.xp: McCoy talked about "ghost musicians" in interviews but named nobody else. The first 5,000 copies carried a cover of Zager and Evans's In the Year 2525.

eras.title: Shows on the death days of magicians
eras.text: McCoy turned the comeback into a calendar: gigs booked on the birth and death dates of people who inspired him, ending in two sold-out nights in London. It took him until 2012 to edit them into a release himself.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: McCoy plays the London Astoria as the Nephilim, first time in seven years
years.p: With Gavin King, Lee Newell, Gizz Butt and Steve Fox-Harris. A year earlier, a European tour had been sold by venues that McCoy said he never confirmed.

years.src: Louder: Fields Of The Nephilim: an interview
years.h: Helsinki, on the anniversary of Rasputin's death
years.p: The start of a run McCoy later admitted was planned to the date: Warsaw on Lovecraft's death day, Athens on the Thelemic new year.
years.xp: "I have never mentioned this to anyone before but I've got a record of a lot of births and deaths of inspirational people," McCoy told Metal Hammer in 2012. "It was part of a bigger plan." Not even his most forensic fans had spotted it, he said.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · Louder: Fields Of The Nephilim: an interview
years.h: Ceromonies sells out Shepherd's Bush Empire twice
years.p: Metal Hammer sponsors two career-spanning nights in London with McCoy, King, Newell, Tom Edwards and Carter. The same line-up headlines M'era Luna in Germany to more than 23,000 people.

years.src: The Quietus
years.h: Opening for [[The Mission|d85e95a3-07c7-4c04-a411-234290615113]]'s 25th birthday at Brixton Academy
years.p: McCoy called it a celebration of the whole goth subculture, not just two bands.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · The Quietus
years.h: Ceromonies (Ad Mortem Ad Vitam), cut by McCoy himself
years.p: The 2008 London shows come out as a double CD and DVD through EMI, with a collector's set in a branded wooden box.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim · The Nefilim: History
years.h: Beggars Archive boxes up the first era
years.p: Dawnrazor, The Nephilim, Elizium and Earth Inferno plus a new singles collection, in one five-album set. Pettitt is back in the band the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Prophecy, the first new song in a decade
years.p: McCoy produces and mixes it himself and puts it out on his own label, Sacred Symphony, after debuting it live in December 2014.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: Guitarist Tom Edwards dies at 41
years.p: Edwards, who played the Ceromonies shows, died of heart failure while touring the US with Adam Ant.

eras.title: Beggars reissues everything
eras.text: Beggars Archive spent three years putting the original albums back out on heavy vinyl, while McCoy's band kept playing live.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fields of the Nephilim
years.h: The Nephilim on golden brown vinyl
years.p: Expanded to a double LP with three bonus tracks. A 30th-anniversary red-vinyl Elizium follows in April 2024, and a Dawnrazor remaster in December 2025.
